2d_tool.spec: One interactive sand-strip the child operates, built ONLY from what this topic's original_chunk prints — 'પશુ, પક્ષી કે માણસના સગડ (પગલાંની છાપ) ઓળખી એ ક્યાંથી આવ્યાં, ક્યાં ગયાં' The screen is a wide strip of smooth pale sand with two control rows under it. Row one, headed કોનાં પગલાં ?, has four Gujarati buttons: માણસ, ઊંટ, બકરી, પક્ષી. Row two, headed ક્યાંથી આવ્યાં, ક્યાં ગયાં ?, has two arrow buttons, ડાબેથી જમણે and જમણેથી ડાબે. WHAT THE CHILD MANIPULATES: the maker and the direction, nothing else. WHAT CHANGES: picking a maker redraws the whole trail across the sand in that maker's own print — a bare human sole in a two-line walking pattern, a broad round camel pad in a long-striding single line, a small cloven goat print, a light three-toed bird track — and picking a direction turns every print in the trail so its toes point that way and moves the freshest, sharpest print to that end of the strip while the far end is drawn wind-blurred. A third button, ઉખેળો, wipes the strip and lays down one trail the child did not build, then asks the two questions the chapter itself asks — કોણ અહીંથી નીકળ્યું ? and એ ક્યાંથી આવ્યું ને ક્યાં ગયું ? — and checks the child's two taps against the trail that was laid, with the topic's own words પગેરું and સગડ shown in the feedback line. LIMIT, deliberately: the chapter also says a પગી can tell age, weight and how long ago the prints were made, but it never prints HOW, so the tool models no mechanism for those and offers no control for them. No digit appears in any display string, and every label the child reads is Gujarati script.
